findings.statement: A positive Staq startup floor plus shared pilot-time scaling improves reserved-family runtime prediction over matched frozen controls.
findings.applicability: Only device-transpilation successful matched tasks forTket/BQSKIT/Staq; no service remote latency. Missing/failed/timeouts excluded from conditional-success runtime target and retained in source audit; cannot infer success probability or realized routing speedup. Author timing environment differs in frequency/run state despite same CPU model.
findings.limitations: The pilot is a measured per-circuit calibration with real computational cost. Only successful matched cases and five held families are tested; no asymptotic-complexity, cross-hardware, quantum-physics or deployed-benefit claim is established. Metric reversal: mean family absolute runtime error is 5.1900 seconds for the reference versus 2.1163 seconds for proportional scaling. The admitted gain concerns relative log error, not uniformly improved error in seconds or measured scheduling time saved.
